name: Shiseido Eudermine

lead:
Eudermine is the product with which Shiseido, a Tokyo pharmacy founded in 1872, entered the cosmetics business in 1897. It is remembered as the starting point of what became one of the world's major beauty companies.
Publicly available histories record the launch date and its significance for the company, but give little detail on the formulation or on measured results.

paras: It was a topical cosmetic lotion applied to the skin as part of a grooming routine. Specific ingredients and directions are not documented in the sources consulted.
No safety data on the original formulation are available. It is no longer a current product in the form described in historical accounts.

chain: Part of an early Japanese skincare routine
angle.text: Eudermine was sold as a cosmetic lotion for the skin. As Shiseido's first cosmetic product, it is part of the history of commercial skincare in Japan.

lead: Eudermine is the lotion that marked Shiseido's entry into cosmetics. According to Wikipedia's article on the company, Shiseido stepped into the world of cosmetics with the introduction of Eudermine in 1897.[1]

Shiseido began as a pharmacy founded in 1872 by Arinobu Fukuhara, a former head pharmacist to the Imperial Japanese Navy.[1] The company later opened a dedicated cosmetics division and cosmetics store in 1916.[1] For people interested in skincare history, Eudermine is the product that links the pharmacy's medicine-making background to a long line of skin products intended to improve complexion and skin condition.
Detailed accounts of the formula, price and customer results are not widely available, so the article is limited to the documented company history.

paras: Shiseido's founder Arinobu Fukuhara, a former head pharmacist to the Imperial Japanese Navy, opened the Shiseido Pharmacy in 1872.[1] The company name comes from the I Ching and refers to praising the virtues of the earth that nurtures new life.[1]

Eudermine was introduced in 1897 and is described as Shiseido's step into cosmetics.[1] Fukuhara's son Shinzo became president in 1913 and emphasised advertising and design, and the company established a cosmetics division and store in 1916.[1]

timeline.event: Arinobu Fukuhara founds the Shiseido Pharmacy.[1]
Shiseido introduces Eudermine, its first cosmetic product.[1]
Shiseido establishes a cosmetics division and store.[1]
